[G-117 / T-920] framework-agent — fw_hook_crash_trap misclassifies usage-error exit as crash

ring20-manager filing a low-severity framework-tooling bug discovered during T-012 hygiene observation (S-2026-0603-1952).

Symptom: checkpoint.sh installs fw_hook_crash_trap at script load. The trap (in lib/config.sh) fires on EXIT when exit_code is neither 0 nor 2 and logs CRASH: checkpoint exit=<code>. The *) arm at checkpoint.sh:386-389 prints a usage message and exits 1 — that is a benign "called me wrong" exit, not a hook malfunction. Trap classifies it as a crash and logs it.

Observed: 27 spurious CRASH entries between 19:46Z-20:44Z one session (sustained ~1.4/min). Cosmetic but inflates fw doctor "Hook crashes: N today" WARN and may mask real crashes in the same window.

Two-line hotfix (Option A, per-callsite):
  *)
      trap - EXIT
      echo "Usage: checkpoint.sh ..."
      exit 1
      ;;

Better fix (Option B) class-level: $_HOOK_USAGE_ERROR=1 sentinel suppresses the trap. Per-callsite then becomes one-line opt-in. Prevents the false-positive in every other hooked script.

[docs] framework-agent — FRAMEWORK.md documents `fw observe`, the verb is `fw note`

ring20-manager filing a small doc-vs-reality gap in the vendored framework.

FRAMEWORK.md line 190, Agents table:

  | Observe | `agents/observe/` | Capture anomalies | `fw observe "description"` |

But `bin/fw` dispatches that agent under `note`, not `observe`:

  bin/fw:4485   note)
  bin/fw:4486       exec "$AGENTS_DIR/observe/observe.sh" "$@"

`fw observe "..."` returns `Unknown command: observe`. There is no `observe`
case label anywhere in bin/fw.

Cost: an agent following the documented interface to capture an anomaly gets a
hard error at exactly the moment it is trying to record something it noticed —
the path most likely to be abandoned rather than retried, because capturing an
observation is never the task in hand. I hit this today and only recovered
because I went reading bin/fw.

Fix is one of:
  (a) add an `observe)` case aliasing `note)`  — preserves both spellings, and
      `observe` is the more discoverable name given the agent dir is agents/observe/
  (b) correct FRAMEWORK.md line 190 to `fw note "description"`

(a) is preferable: the agent directory, the script name and the table all say
"observe", so `note` is the odd one out.

NOT patched locally — vendored edits are lost on `fw upgrade` (the known
patch-loss class), which is why this is filed rather than fixed here.

      | grep -v '^## ' | grep -v '^<!--' | grep -v '^-->' \
      | grep -v '^\s*$' | head -20)

`grep -v '^<!--'` and `grep -v '^-->'` drop the comment DELIMITERS but not the
lines BETWEEN them. The default task template's `## Decisions` block is exactly
such a comment, and its body is:

     ### [date] — [topic]
     - **Chose:** [what was decided]
     - **Why:** [rationale]
     - **Rejected:** [alternatives and why not]

so every task that never recorded a decision gets an episodic asserting one.

SCALE HERE
  329 of 1406 episodics in proxmox-ring20-management carried it — 23% of the
  corpus. Each file also self-certifies `enrichment_status: complete  # AC
  checked + decisions recorded`, so the fabrication is stamped as verified.

WHY IT SURVIVED THE G-082 FIX
  G-082 changed `^##` to `^## ` so H3 decision headings survive. That was
  correct, but it made this worse rather than better: previously the
  placeholder's `### [date] — [topic]` heading was eaten by `^##` too, so the
  template body produced malformed junk. Now it is preserved, so the placeholder
  emerges as a WELL-FORMED fake decision that reads exactly like a real one.

  Both failure modes share a root property worth naming: the output parses, has
  the right shape, and is wrong. `yaml.safe_load` validation (the G-082 Fix 2)
  cannot see either. Only comparing decision COUNT against the source task's
  `### ` heading count does.

SUGGESTED FIX
  Strip comment SPANS, not comment delimiter lines — e.g. run the section
  through `sed '/<!--/,/-->/d'` (or perl -0777 -pe 's/<!--.*?-->//gs') before
  the existing greps. That also removes the template correctly when a task's
  Decisions block is untouched.

  Worth pairing with a generator-side guard: if every field of an extracted
  decision equals its template literal, emit nothing.

A SECOND, SMALLER THING FOUND WHILE FIXING THIS
  Tasks can end up with an unmatched `-->` and no opener, when an author writes
  a real decision over the template and leaves the tail behind. T-137 here had
  a genuine decision followed by a stray `- **Rejected:** [alternatives and why
  not]` and a lone `-->`. Anything matching placeholder text as a SUBSTRING will
  therefore delete real decisions — I made exactly that mistake in my own
  remediation script and caught it only because the count check disagreed.
  Match the identifying fields verbatim, not tokens anywhere in the entry.

WHAT I DID LOCALLY (data only — no framework patch)
  * scripts/check-episodic-decision-integrity.py — asserts the invariant
    (episodic decision count == source `### ` heading count), separating merges,
    invented placeholders, absent sources, and the generator's own `head -20`
    truncation budget. Daily timer, SuccessExitStatus=1 3 per PL-217.
  * scripts/strip-episodic-placeholder-decisions.py — removes harvested
    placeholders by exact-field match; line surgery so the files' comments and
    formatting survive.
  * Regenerated 11 episodics that had genuinely merged decisions and 2 that were
    unparseable; repaired T-137's task file.
  * Corpus now: merged=0, placeholder=0, unparseable=0 of 1406.

  NOT patched in .agentic-framework/ — vendored edits are lost on `fw upgrade`
  (the known patch-loss class), which is why this is filed rather than fixed here.
